title: Driver Voice Radar
description: Ongoing pulse survey capturing driver sentiment on earnings, app stability, and support quality across active markets.
key_findings: App stability complaints dropped 18% after the July release, but remain the #1 driver pain point.
Drivers in Jordan report lower satisfaction with support response time than drivers in KSA (-12 pts).
Earnings predictability, not absolute earnings, is the strongest driver of weekly retention.

title: Driver In-App Reviews
description: Thematic analysis of driver app store and in-app reviews, tagged by sentiment and topic to surface recurring friction points.
key_findings: Payment payout delays are the most cited negative theme (27% of negative reviews).
Navigation/GPS accuracy complaints are concentrated in Amman and Irbid.
Positive reviews increasingly mention the new trip-batching feature.

title: Passenger Activation – No Trips After Sign-Up
description: Behavioral and survey research on passengers who sign up but never complete a first trip, to identify activation blockers.
key_findings: Perceived price uncertainty before requesting a ride is the top-cited activation blocker.
Low driver availability at sign-up time causes immediate drop-off, especially outside Riyadh and Amman.
Passengers who see an upfront fare estimate during onboarding are notably more likely to complete a first trip.

title: Flights Booking Funnel Drop-Off
description: Funnel analysis of the flights booking journey from search to confirmed booking, highlighting where passengers abandon the flow.
key_findings: The largest single drop-off (34%) occurs between fare selection and the payment step.
Passengers comparing multiple fare classes take 3x longer and abandon more often on mobile.
KSA passengers drop off earlier in search; Jordan passengers drop off later, at payment.
